claims.statement: Repeated statements can be judged truer than nonrepeated statements in controlled tasks
claims.limits: Validity judgments, not actual truth or purchases

claims.statement: The 1977 study used three sessions separated by two weeks
claims.limits: Study-specific schedule

claims.statement: Knowledge may be available without being consulted in a truth judgment
claims.limits: Not that knowledge is useless or people lack reasoning

claims.statement: A 2020 Fazio paper assessed prior knowledge before manipulation
claims.limits: Cleaner causal inference about repetition, not purchase intent

claims.statement: Fluency alone explains every truth judgment
claims.limits: Broader framework includes base rates, feelings and consistency with memory

claims.statement: Accuracy focus eliminated illusion in every reader and context
claims.limits: Conditional on relevant knowledge in study

claims.statement: 2020 developmental sample included 24 5-year-olds, 24 10-year-olds, and 32 adults
claims.limits: Small groups, not global prevalence

claims.statement: Does repetition invariably increase factual truth? No. In Corneille's paradigm participants rated whether statements had appeared as fake news on social media; the measure is perceived fakeness, not verified factual accuracy.
claims.limits: The 2022 corrigendum disclosed programming confounds and preregistered robustness studies; cannot generalize to every statement, audience or actual misinformation.

claims.statement: Puységur reports are sources for eighteenth-century suggestion history
claims.limits: Not proof of magnetic fluid or branded self-help results

claims.statement: Zen12 Premium seller advertises 12 levels, 48 MP3 recordings and four styles
claims.limits: No actual purchase/fulfillment

claims.statement: Zen12 seller currently advertises a one-year money-back guarantee
claims.limits: Refund execution unverified

claims.statement: Zen12 seller page showed promotional $87.99 figure on 2026-11-07
